/about: Meta title: About | BonAppé Find
Meta description: Meet BonAppé Find, a restaurant guide that explains the food as well as the address. Learn our story, mission, values and how our data works.
Hero title: About BonAppé Find
Hero subtitle: A restaurant guide that explains the food as well as the address.
Our story

BonAppé Find began with a simple question: why does a restaurant list tell us where to eat, but never how to enjoy it? A name and an address are useful, yet they leave out the stories that make a meal memorable, such as why a dish is served at a certain time, how to share it, or what is polite when the bill arrives.

Four students taking the 6ADDBASE course decided to answer that question. We started with a database of restaurants and built a web application around it. Then we added something most listings forget: the culture. Every country guide in BonAppé Find explains signature dishes, meal times, etiquette, tipping and festivals, and every curated restaurant has a story and a must-order list.
The result is a guide that works for the quick search ("find me a bakery in Brooklyn") and for the curious traveler ("what should I know before dinner in Tokyo?").
Why the name?

BonAppé Find takes its name from bon appétit, the wish we say before a meal, and from the word find. Great dining starts with a great find, so finding the right place is the first course. After that, the story, the dishes and the table manners make the meal.
Our mission
To help people find good restaurants quickly and to make every table feel welcoming by sharing the food culture behind the plate.
Our vision
A world where nobody feels nervous walking into a restaurant, anywhere, because they already know what to order and what to expect.
What we believe
Value | What it means
Respect | We describe every food culture with care and avoid stereotypes.
Clarity | We show the numbers behind every ranking so you can judge for yourself.
Curiosity | We celebrate regional dishes, street food and family kitchens as much as fine dining.
Ownership | Restaurant data should be easy for the people who know it best to correct and update.
What makes us different
Static, hand-written information for every curated restaurant and every country guide.
A transparent Quality Score built from recorded grades.
Full add, edit and delete tools, not just a read-only list.
A design inspired by dark wood, green glass and warm candlelight.
About our data

Most restaurants in BonAppé Find come from the dbRestaurants dataset provided in our course, which covers New York City boroughs. To show how the app works for the world, we added sixteen curated restaurants across eight countries. These sixteen are fictional examples created for this project. Their names, addresses and stories are invented, so please do not try to book them. Always confirm details with a restaurant before you visit.
How it is built
BonAppé Find uses Vue for the interface, Node.js and Express for the API, and MongoDB Atlas for the cloud database. The design was created in Figma.
The team

Abygale Santos and Ayenne Wage designed the experience in Figma. Prince Pangilinan and Casey Ong built the backend and the frontend. Casey Ong also wrote and finalized the documentation, checked every deliverable and manages the repository. Meet everyone on the Team page.

/how-it-works: Meta title: How It Works | BonAppé Find
Meta description: Learn how to search, filter, rank and manage restaurants in BonAppé Find in three easy steps.
Hero title: How BonAppé Find works
Hero subtitle: Three steps from hungry to seated.
Search. Use the search box on the Home or Restaurants page. Pick Name or Cuisine, type a keyword and press Search.
Narrow down. Tap a borough or region button, or choose a country. Open Best Quality to see the top scorers.
Learn and go. Open a profile for the story, signature dishes and grades. Read the country guide for etiquette and tipping.
Use Add a Restaurant to create a listing. On any restaurant row, choose Edit to change details or Delete to remove it. Delete always asks for confirmation first.

When you search or filter, your browser asks the BonAppé Find API for matching restaurants. The API reads MongoDB Atlas and sends back only the records you need, a page at a time. When you add, edit or delete, the API saves the change to Atlas immediately.

Meta description: See the restaurants with the highest combined scores. Aggregated Quality Scores greater than 90, ranked from highest to lowest.
Subtitle: Restaurants whose combined score is greater than 90.

Every time a restaurant is graded, a score is recorded. The Quality Score is the total of all the scores recorded for that restaurant. We add them up in the database, keep the restaurants that total more than 90 points and sort them from highest to lowest. Restaurants with more recorded grades have more chances to build a high total, so check the "Grades recorded" column too.

/faqs: Meta title: FAQs | BonAppé Find
Meta description: Answers to common questions about BonAppé Find, our data, the Quality Score, adding and editing restaurants, and your privacy.
Page title: Frequently asked questions
Subtitle: Quick answers to the things people ask us most.
Search placeholder: Search the FAQs
Categories: General, Data, Using the site, Privacy
Category | Question | Answer

General | What is BonAppé Find? | BonAppé Find is a restaurant discovery web application. You can search restaurants, filter by borough, region or country, see a Quality Score, and read static guides about food culture in eight countries.
General | Is BonAppé Find free? | Yes. BonAppé Find is free to use and you do not need an account to search, browse or read the guides.

General | Who built BonAppé Find? | Four students built it for the 6ADDBASE course: Abygale Santos and Ayenne Wage (design), Prince Pangilinan and Casey Ong (backend and frontend; Casey also handled documentation and project finalization).

Data | Is the restaurant data real? | Most restaurants come from the dbRestaurants dataset provided in our course. The sixteen curated restaurants with full stories are fictional examples created for this project. Always confirm details with a restaurant before you visit.

Data | What do the letter grades mean? | Each grade entry has a date, a letter (A, B, C or Z) and a score. The letter is the label recorded on that date. We show the records exactly as they are stored in the database.

Data | How does the Best Quality ranking work? | We add up every score recorded for a restaurant to get its Quality Score. Restaurants with a total greater than 90 appear on the Best Quality page, from highest to lowest.

Data | Why do restaurants outside New York have a borough? | The borough field is used as a general region field. For New York it holds the borough. For other countries it holds the district, province or region.

Data | How are the country guides written? | Each guide is hand-written by our team using common cultural knowledge about food, meal times, etiquette and festivals. Customs vary by place and by family, so treat the guides as a friendly introduction, not strict rules.
Using the site | How do I search? | Type a keyword in the search box, choose Name or Cuisine, and press Filter. You can also tap a borough button or choose a country to narrow the results.

Using the site | Can I add a restaurant? | Regular users can suggest a restaurant after email verification. Verified, administrator-approved owners can add their own listings. Administrators review suggestions and new owner listings before publication.

Using the site | Can I edit or delete a restaurant? | Yes. Use Edit on any restaurant row or profile to update details. Use Delete to remove a restaurant. Delete asks you to confirm because it cannot be undone.
Using the site | Can I save my favorite restaurants? | Yes. Tap the heart on any restaurant. Your saved list is kept in your own browser and does not need an account.
Using the site | Which browsers does BonAppé Find support? | The latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on desktop, tablet and mobile.
Using the site | I found wrong information. What should I do? | Use the Edit button to fix it, or send us a message from the Contact page and choose Report wrong information.
Privacy | Do I need an account? | No. Accounts are optional and only needed for admin tools. Browsing, searching and reading do not require one.

Privacy | What data do you collect? | We collect only what you send us, such as a contact message, a newsletter email or a review, plus basic technical data. Read the Privacy Policy for the full details.

Guide 1
Field | Content
slug | how-to-read-grades-and-scores
title | How to Read Grades and Scores
excerpt | A quick explanation of letter grades, scores and the Quality Score.
readTimeMinutes | 2
tags | grades, score, quality

body | Every restaurant in BonAppé Find carries a list of grades. Each entry has three parts: a date, a letter grade and a score. The letter (A, B, C or Z) is the label recorded on that date. The score is the number of points recorded with it. On a restaurant profile you will see every entry in a table.

The Quality Score is simple: we add up all of the scores for a restaurant. A restaurant with several strong entries builds a higher total, and any restaurant above 90 points appears on the Best Quality page.

Keep two things in mind. First, totals grow as more grades are recorded, so also look at the Grades recorded column. Second, grades describe the records in our database, not a promise about your meal. Use them as a starting point, then read the story and the country guide.
Guide 2
Field | Content
slug | meal-times-around-the-world
title | Eat Like a Local: Meal Times Around the World
excerpt | Arrive at the right hour and your meal will be much better.
readTimeMinutes | 3
tags | meal times, culture, travel
countrySlug | italy
body | Arriving at the wrong time is the easiest way to find a closed kitchen. Meal times change from country to country, so here is a quick tour.

In Italy, dinner rarely starts before 8 pm. In the United States, many restaurants are busy by 6 pm. In Mexico, the main meal, the comida, is served between 2 and 4 pm. In France and Japan, many restaurants close between lunch and dinner service, so check the hours. In the Philippines, merienda is a beloved afternoon snack, and in India, chai time in the late afternoon comes with small bites. In Thailand, you can eat almost any hour, and night markets come alive after sunset.
Check the opening hours on each restaurant profile, then read the country guide to learn the full rhythm of the day.
Guide 3
Field | Content
slug | tipping-around-the-world
title | Tipping Around the World: A Quick Guide
excerpt | How much to leave, and when to leave nothing at all.
readTimeMinutes | 3
tags | tipping, etiquette, travel
body | Tipping customs can feel confusing, so here is a simple overview. Remember to check the bill first, because a service charge may already be included.

United States: 15 to 20 percent is typical in sit-down restaurants. Mexico: 10 to 15 percent. Philippines: a 10 percent service charge is often added; if not, 5 to 10 percent is appreciated. India: 5 to 10 percent if no service charge is added. Italy: a cover charge (coperto) is common, and a few extra euros for great service is plenty. France: service is included by law, so a small extra is optional. Thailand: not required, but rounding up is appreciated. Japan: do not tip; it can cause confusion, and a polite thank you is best.
When in doubt, ask the staff or follow what locals do.

Meta description: Read the terms that apply when you use BonAppé Find, including rules for adding, editing and deleting restaurant information.
Page title: Terms of Use
Last updated: October 2026
Intro: Welcome to BonAppé Find. Please read these terms carefully. By using this website you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the website.
1. About BonAppé Find

BonAppé Find is an educational web application created by students for the 6ADDBASE course. It lets visitors browse, search and manage restaurant information and read static food guides. It is not a commercial booking, ordering or review platform.
2. Acceptance of these terms

You accept these terms when you open, browse or use any part of BonAppé Find. We may update the terms from time to time. The date at the top shows when they were last changed, and continued use means you accept the updated terms.
3. Who may use the site
BonAppé Find is intended for general audiences. If you are under the age of 18, please use the site with the help of a parent or guardian.
4. Information you add or change
BonAppé Find lets visitors add, edit and delete restaurant records, and post reviews. When you do this, you agree that:
the information is accurate to the best of your knowledge;
you will not submit false, misleading, offensive, hateful or unlawful content;
you will not include private personal data of other people;
you have the right to share any image link or text you provide; and
we may edit, hide or remove content at any time to keep the site accurate and safe.
5. Acceptable use
You agree not to:
attempt to break, overload or gain unauthorized access to the website, the API or the database;
use automated tools to copy large amounts of data without permission;
upload malicious code or links;
impersonate another person or business; or
use the site for any unlawful purpose.
6. Accuracy of information

Most restaurants come from a course dataset. The sixteen curated restaurants with full profiles are fictional examples created for this project, and their names, addresses and stories are invented. Country guides are written as friendly introductions; customs differ between places and families. We do not guarantee that any information is complete, current or correct, so please confirm details with a restaurant before you visit.
7. Quality Score and grades

The Quality Score is a calculation made from the grade records stored in the BonAppé Find database. It is not an official rating or an endorsement of any restaurant, and it may change when records are added, edited or deleted.
8. Intellectual property

The BonAppé Find name, design, layout and original text belong to the project team. Restaurant names and trademarks belong to their owners. You may view and share the site for personal, non-commercial and educational purposes. You may not copy the design or text for commercial use without permission.
9. Links to other websites
BonAppé Find may link to websites that we do not control. We are not responsible for their content or practices.
10. Suspension and removal
We may suspend access, remove content or block users who break these terms, at our discretion.
11. Disclaimer
BonAppé Find is provided "as is" and "as available". We make no promise that the site will always be available, error-free or secure, or that it will meet your needs.
12. Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent allowed by law, the BonAppé Find team is not liable for any loss or damage that comes from using, or being unable to use, the website or from relying on its information, including any decision about where to eat.
13. Governing law
These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of the Philippines.

Questions about these terms? Contact us at hello@bonappefind.example or through the Contact page.

/privacy: Meta title: Privacy Policy | BonAppé Find
Meta description: Learn what information BonAppé Find collects, how we use it and the choices you have.
Page title: Privacy Policy
Last updated: October 2026

Intro: Your privacy matters to us. This policy explains what information BonAppé Find collects, why we collect it, how we protect it and what choices you have. We follow the principles of transparency, legitimate purpose and proportionality found in the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (Republic Act No. 10173) of the Philippines.
1. Who we are
BonAppé Find is a student project created for the 6ADDBASE course. The project team is the controller of the information described below. You can reach us at hello@bonappefind.example.
2. Information we collect
We collect only what we need:
Contact form: your name, email address, subject and message.
Newsletter: your email address and the date you subscribed.
Reviews: the display name and comment you choose to post.
Accounts (optional): your name, email address and a password stored only in encrypted (hashed) form.
Restaurant records: the restaurant details you add or edit. Please do not include personal information about private individuals.
Technical data: browser type, device type, pages visited and error logs, collected by our hosting services to keep the site working.
Browser storage: your saved restaurants and display preferences, kept only in your own browser.
3. How we use your information
We use your information to:
reply to your messages;
send the newsletter you asked for;
show your reviews and restaurant changes on the site;
let you log in and use admin tools if you have an account;
keep the website secure and fix errors; and
understand which features are useful so we can improve them.
4. Why we may process your information

We process your information with your consent (for example, when you subscribe or send a message), to provide the features you request, and for our legitimate interest in running and securing the website.
5. Who we share it with

We do not sell your personal information. We share it only with service providers that help us run the site, such as our database host (MongoDB Atlas), our website and API hosts and our email delivery service. These providers may only use the information to provide their services to us. We may also disclose information if the law requires it.
6. How long we keep it

Contact messages are kept for up to twelve months. Newsletter emails are kept until you unsubscribe. Reviews and restaurant records stay until they are deleted. Account details are kept until you ask us to delete your account.
7. How we protect it

We use secure connections (HTTPS), hashed passwords, input validation, rate limiting and limited access to the database. No system is completely secure, so please use a strong, unique password if you create an account.
8. Your rights
You have the right to:
be informed about how your data is used;
access the information we hold about you;
ask us to correct inaccurate information;
ask us to delete your information or block its use;
object to certain uses of your information, such as the newsletter;
receive a copy of your information in a common format; and
file a complaint with the National Privacy Commission of the Philippines.
To use any of these rights, contact us at hello@bonappefind.example. We will respond within a reasonable time.
9. Children
BonAppé Find is not designed to collect information from children under 13. If you believe a child has sent us personal information, please contact us and we will delete it.
10. Cookies and local storage
We use only simple browser storage to remember your saved restaurants and preferences. Read our Cookie Policy for details.
11. Links to other sites
Other websites linked from BonAppé Find have their own privacy policies. We are not responsible for them.
12. Changes to this policy
We may update this policy. When we do, we will change the date at the top of this page.
13. Contact us
For privacy questions, write to hello@bonappefind.example or use the Contact page.
Notice for the team: This Privacy Policy is a template written for a student project. Review it with a qualified professional before any public launch, and keep it matching what the code really does.
/cookies: Meta title: Cookie Policy | BonAppé Find
Meta description: How BonAppé Find uses cookies and browser storage.
Intro: This page explains what cookies and browser storage are, which ones BonAppé Find uses and how you can control them.
What are cookies and local storage?
Cookies are small text files saved by your browser. Local storage is a similar space inside your browser that lets a website remember information on your device.
bonappefind_saved | Local storage | Remembers the restaurants you saved | Until you clear it
bonappefind_compare | Local storage | Remembers restaurants chosen for comparison | Until you clear it
bonappefind_token | Local storage (only if you log in) | Keeps you logged in | Up to 7 days
bonappefind_consent | Local storage | Remembers that you have read this notice | 12 months
BonAppé Find does not use advertising cookies and does not track you across other websites.
You can delete cookies and local storage in your browser settings at any time. If you do, your saved list and comparison will be removed.
Banner text: BonAppé Find keeps your saved restaurants in your browser. We do not use advertising cookies. Buttons: Got it, Read the Cookie Policy
/accessibility: Meta description: Our commitment to making BonAppé Find usable by everyone.
Intro: We want everyone to be able to find a good meal. BonAppé Find is designed to be usable with a keyboard, a screen reader and on small screens.
Use text and background colors with strong contrast.
Show grades with a letter as well as a color.
Provide alternative text for images and a text table for each chart.
Make every button and link reachable with the keyboard and show a clear focus outline.
Offer a skip link to go straight to the main content.
Use a responsive layout that works from 360 pixels wide.
Photos added by users through image links may not include a description. Some charts may be harder to read on very small screens, which is why a data table is always provided.
Tell us how we can improve
If you find something hard to use, please write to hello@bonappefind.example. We will do our best to fix it.
